newsitem.title: UK: BNFL trims request for hike in discharge limits.
newsitem.headline: BNFL trims request for hike in discharge limits.

text.p: British Nuclear Fuels (BNFL) said on Friday it had trimmed back the cuts requested in pollution controls for its Thermal Oxide Reprocessing Plant (Thorp) as a result of further improvements.
BNFL had asked for an increase in aerial discharge limits for tritium at Thorp, in Cumbria, north west England, last November.
But BNFL said since then, experience of operating Thorp at higher throughput levels and further improvements in gaseous clean-up systems "has shown that the increase will not be required."
It had also requested an increase in the limits for discharge of Iodine 129 from the High Level Waste plants area, but said now it intended to reduce the allowance sought.
BNFL said the Environment Agency had been told of the new position and asked to reconsider the application. BNFL said it now expected a period of public consultation.
The Environment Agency needs to balance the dangers of discharges against the benefits of recovering plutonium and uranium from spent fuel which will be stockpiled.
BNFL's original requests for an increase in its limits was seen as necessary to allow Thorp to operate at full capacity. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
